brief.headline: Fix the 40% return rate first, then push price toward ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume

priceAsk.summary: Target ₹0.65–0.80/pc for 28 mm caps at higher volume or looser spec
priceAsk.basis: Market asking price is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc; verdict says MARKET-FAIR with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec — we should capture that headroom

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep current 30 Days After Receipt; do not offer faster payment until returns drop below 10%

brief.financialLeverage: Scorpion publishes no financials, so we can't see their revenue, profit or cash position. Our ₹1.66 L annual spend is tiny — we have zero scale leverage here. The real leverage is quality: 40% of their deliveries come back, so they're bleeding cost on rework and freight. They need this business to run clean more than they need a price fight. Line up a second source (Manjushree or Mold-Tek) to show we can walk if quality and price don't both improve.

evidence.point: Four out of every ten deliveries get returned or reversed
Our annual spend with them is very small
Market asking price for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps runs ₹0.55–1.20 per piece, typically ₹0.85–0.95
Market verdict says price is fair but there's modest room to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec
evidence.figure: MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec

evidence.point: HDPE resin import unit value (a raw-material benchmark) is 87.61 ₹/kg

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; revenue ₹2569.83 Cr, health score B (65/100) — top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers, pharma packaging; revenue ₹946.50 Cr, health score B (73/100) — robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited
alternates.why: Manufacturer lead for rigid plastics, pan-India presence — a lead to qualify (verify capability and MOQ before RFQ)

risks: 40% return rate means half their shipments waste our receiving time and their freight — push a joint quality plan (tighter inspection at their dock, spec review) before any price or volume commitment
We spend only ₹1.66 L/year with them — we're a tiny customer, so they won't bend much on price unless we bundle volume or offer a longer contract
No public financials — we can't tell if they're stable or struggling, so keep Manjushree or Mold-Tek warm as a backup in case Scorpion stumbles
If they can't fix returns, the 'cheap' price becomes expensive once you add the cost of our time sorting out reversals — quality is the real negotiation here
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We want to keep working with you, but 40% of your deliveries come back — let's fix that first, then talk about hitting ₹0.70/pc at higher, defect-free volume.
